page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.55 GHz. It provisions 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware instruction set support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA cryptography extensions.

The hardware configuration features 64 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, requiring external cloud storage for file systems and database persistence. Network connectivity is configured with a 7 Gbps baseline throughput profile. In throughput tests, cached memory operations demonstrate substantial speeds, while uncached streaming bandwidth measures lower at 39.33 GB/sec read and 18.82 GB/sec write.

Benchmark results place the ecs.g7a.4xlarge squarely in mid-tier performance categories for compute and data processing. Stress-ng returned 2677.3 on single-core and 21587.12 on multi-core execution, while Geekbench recorded 1536.0 single-core and 8861.0 multi-core scores. In operational benchmarks, the instance sustained 15.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.72 GB/sec in static web serving tests. PassMark memory testing showed upper-quartile responsiveness at 2753.61 points.

By delivering standard resource symmetry without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware or bundled physical disks, the instance provides steady resource efficiency for general production systems. The ecs.g7a.4xlarge is designed for distributed microservices, application backends, web serving tiers, Redis caching nodes, and network-attached database servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7a.4xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance equipped with 16 vCPUs across 8 dedicated AMD EPYC 7T83 physical cores clocked at 2.55 GHz and 64 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it offers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without integrated GPU hardware or local disk storage, operating on a 7 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate balanced mid-tier compute capabilities, recording 21587.12 in stress-ng multi-core and 8861.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, paired with strong PassMark memory performance. While uncached memory throughput exhibits lower bandwidth limits, cache operations remain competitive, supporting 15.73 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.72 GB/sec static web serving. This configuration provides dependable resource efficiency for general business applications, containerized environments, caching layers, and web application deployments backed by cloud storage.
